public_rationale: OpenAI's August 7, 2025 disclosure reports GPT-5 matching or exceeding experts in roughly half the cases on an internal benchmark spanning over 40 occupations; this supports a limited shortfall from universal expert competence [e1]. The July 2023 study summary reports 40% less completion time and 18% higher quality on selected writing tasks, showing gains without demonstrating tenfold whole-worker productivity [e2]. These findings do not cover the full set of expectations or establish ChatGPT's overall record against them through November 29, 2025 [e1, e2].
limitations: The capability comparison is company-reported and limited to its internal benchmark.
The writing experiment concerns selected tasks and a 2023 version of ChatGPT, not representative whole-worker productivity at publication.
The packet does not adequately cover AGI or the one-person billion-dollar company example.
The cited expectations' intended delivery dates and weighting are not established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT has not lived up to expectations.

statement.excerpt: And I certainly don’t think that ChatGPT has lived up to expectations.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: anything a PhD student could do
a billion dollar company run by just a single employee
our_interpretation: The plain contextual reading concerns the strong expectations listed immediately afterward, not every user's expectations or whether ChatGPT has any value.
The target is ChatGPT's record from its stated launch through publication on 2025-11-29.
Tenfold productivity means ten times comparable output per unit of labor, with quality accounted for.
An expectation not yet delivered by publication is distinct from a forecast whose deadline has expired. The end of 2025 had not arrived.
An overall verdict needs evidence covering the cited expectations; isolated task results cannot establish the whole comparison.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from the target period establishes that ChatGPT had materially fallen short of the cited expectations of broad human or PhD-level competence and transformative worker-level productivity, with adequate coverage of the other cited outcomes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence from the target period establishes delivery of the cited capabilities and productivity outcomes at their stated breadth, rather than isolated demonstrations or selected tasks.

evidence.explanation: The publisher reports meaningful improvements in professional writing tasks, below a tenfold time-productivity improvement. This supports the narrower shortfall on those tasks, but neither measures whole jobs nor establishes the performance of late-2025 ChatGPT.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Documented expectations with their intended delivery dates, together with evaluations and verifiable outcome records through November 29, 2025 covering broad competence, representative worker productivity, AGI, and the one-person company example.
